scores.why: Yardstick: the bright green wash with one colour of everything else, which is the 'nearly identical, too contrasty' page the owner has been asking to move away from.
Desk Terminal Banded is grounded and tidy, with a real tube and a faint row band, but it is the same pewter-and-mono desk the owner has seen, and it has none of the line art they love.

The Fraunces serif titles, cream ink on a teal-black ground, the dotted rails for To do and Coming up, and the chat thread hanging from Vera's mark all change the whole page, and it keeps the glowing Next up tube.
Its tube has a good scope and the count strip is useful, but a pewter table-and-mono page with a green wash is closer to today than the leaders are.

The drafting-sheet idea, with a grid, title block, dashed ways to start and hatched swatches, is a very different page that still has a glowing tube, but the title blocks and the scalloped bubbles are busy for the family.

Fine rails with a lit NOW dot lead the eye down every page, section heads sit on the rails with serif titles and small coloured tabs, and the tube glows on the rail; this is the Signal Box line language the owner praised, carried through all the pages.
A brass-and-manila catalogue with brown frames and tan plates: the owner already called brown borders off-motif and warm browns not CRT, and the page drags the green into the background.
An early Desk Terminal with a tube holding the question; it is clean and grounded but plain, and it has no line art or distinctive type.
The same Desk Terminal with raised select keys and a firmer row band; a small change that the owner will not see at a glance across the page.

Thin section-coloured rules and big light numerals do put colour and variation across the page, but the colours are the familiar violet, cyan and lemon on the same desk page, and the numerals fight the titles.

It is the strongest Track Diagram: bigger display-serif titles, a chat that opens on a headed question with 'mind' lit, and a quiet Ready fold on the tube; it has real typographic care and the rail line art, and it adds no new colour.

A typed count in each page's own colour beside the serif title, a lit status line on the glass and a cooler ground with warmer ink; the colour and type changes are small but they show on every page head.
A tray of big-figure tiles and a steady block cursor make a better count strip, but it is still the pewter table page, and the strip is tall and has empty arrow tiles.
A tallied numeral and a lamp line are good small ideas, but this is the plain Long Persistence page with few new marks and the same Matrix-adjacent green.

The blueprint's grid and frames in violet, amber and cyan pencil, rules ending in solid blocks, and lit words on the live list make colour a feature on every sheet while the tube keeps the glow, though the pencil is faint at card size.
Cool slate under warm bone words and banded ledger rows are quiet and well judged, but the change is subtle and the bone text looks white at card size.

The Grid Console with a round lit NOW lamp on a lit rail, a pilot lamp in the footer and a phosphor gauge on Status; the lit marks are the glowing dots on black that the owner says made the original unique, and they sit on fine rails.

A bold Home question with 'mind' in a three-layer halo, one-line page heads and light numerals show in the first screen, but the line-art language is the same as its parent's and the changes are modest.
The gauge and shaped lamps are fine ideas, but they sit on the brown manila catalogue that the owner finds off-motif.
Titled rules with coloured light rails are the best thing in the Catalogue line and calm it a little, but the brass and tan plates are still the problem.

A printed-timetable page with huge thin numerals, flush-left Inter, steel-blue time and lit phosphor only for the machine is a genuinely different page that fixes the wash, but it loses much of the CRT soul and the line art, and it has 41 small targets on Home.

fixes.suggestion: Keep the display serif, the headed chat opening and the Ready fold. Add Grid Console's lit NOW dot on the Coming up rail and a visible count beside the page titles so the Home page changes more than the heads.

Keep the NOW lamp with the time on its own glass, the footer pilot lamp and the gauge. Show the gauge as a tube in the Status head only when it has something to read, so it does not sit at $0.00 and make the head twice as tall.

Keep the typed count in each page's colour and the lit status line on the glass. Put the count on a quieter baseline on Plans and Ideas, where the head is crowded, and push the cooler ground slightly further so it shows.
Keep the rails and the NOW dot, which the owner loves. Add the halo and pilot light from mut-9 and ease the dense hatched placeholder cells in the Finish setting up row.

Keep the huge thin section numerals, the heavy coloured opening rules and phosphor-only-on-the-machine. Bring back the rail line art and a visible halo on the lit marks and the tube, and raise the 41 small targets on Home to 44px.
Keep the per-sheet pencil colours and the solid end blocks. Make the pencil lines a step stronger so they show at half size, and drop the busy title block and scalloped bubbles.
Take the titled rule with a trailing coloured light rail to a grounded teal-black case instead of the brown catalogue. The rail is good; the manila and brass are what fail.

judges.notes: The leaders are the two line-art families, Track Diagram (mut-3, mut-4, head-1) and Grid Console (mut-9, head-3, mut-10). Both carry the rails and subway lines the owner called high style through every page, with serif headings, cream ink on a teal-black ground, and a tube whose glow is kept for the monitors and the lit marks. They differ from today on every page, not in a corner. Blueprint is next: it is a strong different idea with colour, but busy. The Desk Terminal and Long Persistence variants are tasteful and grounded but still read as today's page with extra pewter, and their changes are small. Signal Catalogue and its children are scored low because their brass, manila and tan are the browns the owner has said do not fit the CRT motif. Swiss Thread is the boldest new idea and answers 'nearly identical', but it costs the CRT soul, the lines and the target sizes, so it is a promise vote rather than a finalist by score. The mut-9 NOW lamp, the pilot lamp and the lit rail are the best glowing-dots-on-black idea this round.

parts.what: Next up tube sitting on the rail with a faint scale below, plus a lit status line under the question
Coming up as dated plates hanging from a lit NOW rail; To do as dotted rail with the due time in the margin
Thread hanging from Vera's mark, opening on a headed question with 'mind' lit and times in the margin
Teal-black ground with warm cream ink, plus thin section-coloured lines and sage and cyan companions
Fraunces display serif page titles at large optical size over mono labels and sans body
White-hot NOW lamp on a lit rail, a footer pilot lamp, and a halo only on the live words

scores.why: The true tube light (halo on 'mind', glowing monitors, lit dots) is all there, but it is a monochrome wash with nothing the family hasn't seen.
The question is typed on the glass beside Next up and Status gets a lit dial gauge in VT323, so the tube's bloom, scanlines and glowing figures carry real page content while the case stays grounded.

Home is one real green screen with VERA, the typed question, Next up and the scope inside, and grounded bands outside, which keeps the soul in the right place; Status's $0.00 readout and bar are a lesser echo of the dial.
Same convincing tube as Banded, with raised select keys and serif headings that are not visible at the heads and add no light, so the soul equals the parent and the difference is quiet.
Banded's tube soul plus a greener glass against a steel-teal case and thin coloured section lines make the screen more of a lit object against a calmer case, though the change is still subtle.
The vertical phosphor beam and condensed type give the monitor real afterglow, but the Status head is a bare line of text and the page outside the tube goes flat.
It keeps the scope's beam and halo and adds a tile tray, but the stepped-down question with a green block cursor drifts toward the Matrix terminal look and Status is still empty.
The mono lamp line is a nice small signal, but only its idle state shows and Status remains a bare paragraph; the tube is unchanged.

The cream serif title, glowing nodes on the rail and the halo around the question box are a grounded, lit page, but the monitor is the only tube and the glow is spread thinner than on the Desk Terminal.
Display-size serif titles are handsome typesetting but add no light; the Ready fold appears nowhere in the close crops.
The typed count beside each serif title and the lit lamp status line under the question add small live signals that read on every page, though the cooler ground barely registers.

Green-black glass over a drafting grid with the lit 'MIND' and a status line inside the tube is distinctive and still unmistakably a phosphor screen, though the sheet-and-note frames feel more like paper than a tube.
A two-layer halo on the live list's lit words and pencil-coloured rule ends bring light and colour to the content, but the Ideas and Status heads still read as the parent.
Bone-white words on cooler slate and lamp legend are tasteful, but the warmth is almost invisible and the tube light is unchanged.
Faint scanned grid lines run the page, serif titles in cream, a lit nav underline and a floor grid inside the tube make the whole page feel powered rather than one corner.
A lit rail with a round NOW lamp and a pilot lamp on the footer horizon is a good powered-console idea, but the Status head crop shows an empty gap where the gauge should be.

Home's question is a bold panel with a three-layer halo on 'mind' and a bright Send, and the one-line head keeps the grid-console glow while the monitor keeps its bloom; light shows where attention goes.

The tube in its wood bezel with the lit ECG trace is the most vivid screen in the field, but brass plates, brown ground and mono type turn the page into a steampunk catalogue, away from the green-screen motif.
The brass catalogue look hides the green with a lamp key, and the gauge is not visible in the Status crop, which leaves the tube lonely.
A brass rail in the section colour is a tidy structural idea, but it reads as the old brass underline and adds no phosphor.

Phosphor is deliberately confined to the mark, Send, key word, focus and the tube, with huge thin numerals and square corners; it is bold and not Matrix, but most of the page is white-on-black grotesque and the halo on 'mind' is strong enough to threaten glare.

fixes.suggestion: Keep the typed question, Next up and the dial gauge on one tube; restore the dial to Status in the Banded line, which dropped it for a plain $0.00 bar, and keep halo only on the key word and the needle.
Keep the section-coloured top lines and greener glass, but push the case tint further so the difference shows on the cards; reconsider the 40px numeral so it doesn't outrank the band title.
Bring back the spend dial from the Joined parent on Status, keeping the grounded bands.
Keep the bold lit 'mind' panel and the one-line head, and carry the same three-layer halo to a single live word per page so the light is a system and not a Home trick.
Keep the 'light only where the machine is' rule and the thin numerals, but warm the white headings to bone so Matrix-white doesn't return, and soften the 'mind' halo on the big title.
The lit rail with a round NOW lamp and the footer pilot lamp are the right size of idea; show the gauge in the head at a size that does not leave a gap, and set the needle to a believable value.
Keep the wood-bezel monitor with the ECG trace as the screen; swap the brass plates and brown ground for the slate neutrals so the green stays the page's light.

judges.notes: The strongest soul comes from putting content on the glass: the Desk Terminal family sets the question, Next up and the spend dial inside a real tube, so bloom, scanlines and phosphor figures belong to the page content and the case stays grounded. Grid Console and Blueprint spread a quiet power through the page (grid lines, lit rails, a nav underline) without glare. The serif Folio and Track Diagram line is calmer and handsomely typeset, but its tube light is the same as today's. Signal Catalogue has the best single tube but loses the green motif to brass and brown. Swiss Thread is the freshest idea and nothing like the Matrix, but needs warmth in its whites and fewer halos to keep the glow scarce. Several mutants look identical to their parents on the close cards, which the owner's latest word would punish.

parts.what: three-layer halo on the one lit word 'mind' in the Home panel, bright Send, halo kept for the live word only
one tube holding the VERA line, Next up, scope and the typed question in VT323
serif title with a typed count in the page colour standing on the masthead rule; wild-1 uses a huge thin section numeral
lit nodes strung on a vertical rail; the lamp status line under the question
moving-coil spend dial in phosphor with a limit mark on the Status tube, with the $0.00 VT323 readout

scores.why: Recognisable green-screen identity with real bloom, but one hue, one rhythm and one card shape everywhere; it is the Matrix the family named.
The Home tube column beside a plain content column is a clear idea, but it is flat, dull below the fold, and the list pages are a stock dark table.
The same desk terminal with a typed-question tube and a numbered timeline spine in Chat. Tidy and more grounded, but unmemorable and still a lot like today.
The scope trace and the tally strip give the tube a job, but the page is mostly today's cards with a ruled strip added.
Serif titles, a colour-coded track-diagram spine and tinted idea cards give an editorial railway-timetable feel; the Chat thread on a vertical line is lovely, and it shows on every page.
The drafting-sheet identity is the most complete: grid, title block, lit keys, scalloped revision-cloud bubbles and a bezelled tube. It is distinctive, but its mono caps are dense.
Perspective floor, lit rail with node marks, serif section heads and a NOW stamp. It feels like a powered console with a clear point of view, and the typesetting is good.
The brass and manila catalogue with waveform traces and hot lamps is a bold material idea and warm against the green. It leans brown and costume-like, and the Home tail is cramped.
The serif headings are nearly invisible on these cards and the band is subtle, so almost nothing is new over the Desk Terminal parent.
The coloured section rules and large count numerals add visible variety across the pages. The change is still thin and the numeral outranks the title.
Display-size Fraunces titles and a headed 'Vera asks / What's on your mind?' opening on the Chat thread are a real typographic lift. The Ready-line fold is not visible on these cards.

A typed count in the page's colour beside the serif title (the violet 12 on Ideas, the '2 replies' beside Vera) is a charming editorial detail. The status line under the question adds life, and the cooler ground and warmer ink help.
The tile tray with big figures and the steady cursor add some structure, but the tray repeats the sections and is crowded, and the cursor edges toward the Matrix look.
The lamp line and the tally numerals are tasteful but small. This is the parent page with garnish.

Each sheet's hairlines and solid end blocks are drawn in its own pencil (cyan, violet, pink, yellow), so colour structure shows across the page and the lit words keep their glow. It is the Blueprint at its best.
Warm bone words on cooler slate with ledger bands is a gentle, grounded move. It is correct but quiet; the half-size cards show little over the parent.

A round white-hot NOW lamp on a lit rail with its own time glass, and a pilot lamp at the footer horizon, make the console visibly powered. The Status gauge is a good idea but its close card does not show it.
A bold lit question as one panel, a one-line page head, and light Fraunces numerals a size up are real typesetting care on top of the strongest console. The ideas card grid reads well.
The phosphor gauge and shape-coded lamps are good instrument ideas on a brass catalogue. The page reads the same as its parent, and the gauge is not shown on Home.
The titled rule with a coloured trailing rail replaces the manila plates, and the page is calmer and more structured. The effect is faint on the cards.

A Swiss timetable with a terminal in it: huge thin numerals in section colours, flush-left grotesque type, ruled rows, and a three-column Home with the question as the loudest thing. It is a genuinely new identity with the phosphor lit only where the machine is. Contrast and target size need work.

fixes.suggestion: Keep the huge thin numerals, section-coloured heavy rules and the question as the loudest thing. Fix min text contrast (4.77), raise the 41 sub-44px targets, and add back some halo and glow on the lit words and tube. Level the three Home column ends and give the thread more than 24 hours.

Keep the per-sheet pencil colours and solid end blocks, which are the first colour in this line that the family would see across pages. Make the pencil lines stronger on Ideas and Plans and extend the pencil to Chat and Status. Add a little more type contrast to the mono caps.

Keep the single-panel question with the three-layer halo on 'mind', the one-line head and the light Fraunces numerals. Make sure 300-weight numerals stay legible at 11-12px, and give the panel frame a more distinct personality from the parent.
Keep the NOW lamp on the lit rail and the footer pilot lamp. The gauge needs a non-zero demo value so the needle reads, and it should be a compact element rather than doubling the Status head height.
Keep the typed coloured count beside the serif title and the status line. Make the cooler ground more perceptible and keep the head from getting crowded on Plans and Ideas.
Keep the lamp, waveform and brass-plate vocabulary but pull the brown toward a cooler brass so the page is not muddy. Use the manila plate only for page titles, and fix the cramped Home tail.

judges.notes: The field splits into five families: Desk Terminal (calm, closest to today), Track Diagram (serif and timeline), Blueprint (drafting sheet), Grid Console (powered rail and floor) and Signal Catalogue (brass plates). Plus Swiss Thread, which is the one clean-sheet design. The Desk Terminal and Long Persistence lines look too much like today, so they score low on the owner's 'nearly identical' test. The strongest creative identities are Blueprint, Grid Console and Swiss Thread, and each shows across every page: title blocks, a rail with nodes, huge thin numerals. Track Diagram's serif and spine add editorial warmth. Signal Catalogue is bold but its brass can look muddy. The owner's wish to bring back the halo and bloom is best met in the Console line (lit 'mind', tube, rail glow) and in Blueprint's lit keys. Swiss Thread risks under-delivering that light but compensates with a real sense of design. I score the line-up on how much of the page content changes and how much character it has.

parts.what: Inter with an optical size, huge thin section numerals, Geist Mono small caps at 0.72rem; or light Fraunces figures a size above their text
Green-black glass in a steel-slate case, with each sheet's hairlines drawn in its own pencil colour (cyan, violet, pink, amber)
Huge thin numeral in the section colour with a flush-left bold title and grey lede; or the drafting title block with SHEET, NOTE, DO and NO. cells and the primary key in it
Section rule ending in a solid coloured block, in the section's pencil; or a titled rule trailing a lit rail
Bezelled tube with a readout line inside ('4 plans · 3 late · Vera is listening'); or a status line with a lit lamp under the question
A single pilot lamp lit on the footer horizon with a lit run either side; or a numbered top bar with a lit segment under the mark

scores.why: Clear and usable but one flat green; the question box and Send are findable, though starters are pale and the page reads as one glow with no hierarchy beyond it.
Question lives on the tube and the composer below; large targets (0 under 44) and clear tab bar, but the glass crowds the first screen and the question is mono-green rather than the lead.
Tube first, then one composer with a bright Send; reads title, action, content; big targets, banded rows help scanning, but looks close to the old page.
Calm folio type and a clean select, but Home is almost identical to today and the Next up tube wraps its title into three lines.
Competent Vera box and scope tube, tally strip adds some glance value; still visually the present page with a tweak.

Coherent drafting-sheet system: caps labels, FROM bar joined to the box, dashed starters, numbered menus and selects; labels are small and the box edge-to-edge feels cramped but the rules would hold on any page.
Strong structure: full-width starter rows with generous targets, a clean label/field/Send line, caps Send; starters are heavy in height and push the tube down.
Warm brown ground with keyed tab bar and clear Vera card is the most visibly different and grounded; select popup with active dot is well done; brown is slightly muddy at night.
Raised-key select with a flipping chevron and bolder serif keys improve the control read, but the rest is the Banded page and the bands add little.
Short rule under the current tab is a good wayfinding cue and thin section lines add structure, but on Home the change is subtle and the phone view is unchanged otherwise.
Display serif titles help hierarchy, but Home on the phone is nearly the same as its parent and the Ready fold does not show on Home.
The status line under the question (listening, watching 4 plans) answers the glance question well; ground change is too slight to see.
Smaller question and steady cursor are fine, the tray strip is useful, but Home looks like its parent and the cursor leans Matrix.
The mono lamp line says whether anything waits and the select reads as a button, a real usability gain, but the caps line is small and the page is otherwise unchanged.
Same sound Blueprint system with pencil-coloured sheets and bigger rule ends; Home matches head-2 so the gain shows on other pages.
Blueprint with warm bone words and bands; sound, but the card is indistinguishable from head-2 and the banding is faint.
Grid Console with a pilot lamp and gauge keeps the neat starter rows and Send; Home is the same as head-3 and the gauge only helps Status.

One panel with bold question, a sentence-case From bar and compact outlined starters gives the best phone Home of the Grid line: title, one action, content; the serif 'Finish setting' heading wraps awkwardly at the fold.
Catalogue with a raised select key and gauge; same warm system as head-4 with a slightly heavier select that reads as pressable, but nothing new on Home.
Calmer Catalogue with titled rules and bare footer, reads cleanly; Home matches head-4 and the rule change shows below the fold.

Largest hierarchy change on the page: giant question, flush-left grotesque, thread and ruled rows with phosphor only on the mark, key word, Send and focus; the squint is clear and it reads across pages, though many targets are under 44px and Home thread is thin.

fixes.suggestion: Keep the large lead question, flush-left grotesque and the phosphor reserved for the mark, key word, Send and focus; raise the many small targets to 44px (starters, From select, checkbox row) and show more than the last day of the thread so Home does not read empty.

Keep the one-panel composer and compact outlined starters; fix the wrapped serif 'Finish setting' heading at the fold (let it span one line or drop to the sans) and keep the light numerals only at sizes where weight 300 stays readable.
Keep the warm keyed tab bar and the Vera card; lift the brown a touch toward a graphite-umber so it stays grounded at night, and give the tab keys a clearer pressed state for the current page.
Keep the numbered menus, dashed starters and joined From/Send bar; relax the edge-to-edge box with a little side padding and lift the 12px caps labels so they hold on a phone at night.

The short rule under the current tab and section-coloured top lines are the right system cues; make the section colour lines 2px and visible on Home, not just half-strength, so the change is seen across the page.
Lift the lamp line out of 13px caps mono into a readable size and keep it as the Home glance; the plain-button select is worth carrying to every candidate.

judges.notes: Most of the field is variations on four parents (Desk Terminal, Track Diagram, Blueprint, Grid Console) that look the same on Home at card size, so the owner's 'nearly identical' complaint applies to many of them. Swiss Thread is the one design whose whole Home hierarchy changes (giant question, then Send, then content), and the squint reads title, action, content cleanly; it loses points on target size (41 of 55 under 44px). The Grid Console single panel and the warm Signal Catalogue are the best of the carried lines for a first-time family member on a phone. Desk Terminal variants have the best targets (0 under 44) but put the glass above the composer, which delays the one action. Gauge and count-strip ideas help Status but not Home, so they cannot lift a score on this card.

parts.what: raised graphite select key with a steel chevron that flips open onto a plain plate list, plus a brighter raised Send
phone tab bar with the current page marked by a short coloured rule under its label; keyed tab bar as runner
one mono lamp line under the question saying what Vera is doing and whether anything waits
one panel with bold question and lit key word, a From bar with mic and Send, then compact outlined starters
flush-left bold grotesque title leading the page with a grey lede and section-coloured numeral; count beside the title as runner

scores.why: Yardstick: it keeps the tube's real glow, but it is a green wash on black with no companions and a card-grid sameness. It is the Matrix reading the family named.
The steel case and banded rows are a real change and the sidebar tube is lit, but the page is a sidebar plus a slab, and the chrome is a lot of grey plates.

Fraunces titles, the To do timeline spine with dated nodes and a lit NOW, the week dial and tinted page glyphs change the content on every page. The ground is a touch flat, and the Status tube is cut off on the card.
The scope on To do is strong, but Status and Settings are close to today's page. The count strip is a tab row, and the lighting is only slightly refined.
The blueprint sheet frame, grid and numbered sheets are bold and carry the whole page. The all-caps tracked heads are dense and shouty, and the faint cyan grid risks an editor-theme feel.

Serif titles with titled rails, a calm card grid, a hatched past, a lit NOW and a today box in warm amber carry across all four pages. The phosphor stays on the rails and the bar, and the page is calm.
The brass manila labels and brown ground are a bronze wash: a costume of a card catalogue, and the green is lost on Plans and To do.
The gauge in the sidebar tube is fine, but the page is a dark slab with a tube in a corner and little else. It is a bar to beat, not a destination.
This is Banded plus serif section heads and stripes. The near-duplicate of mut-3 reads as a modest typographic gain, and the raised keys are invisible in the card.
The section-coloured hairlines and big numerals are too faint to see at card size. It is essentially the parent, with a numeral that duplicates the contents plate.
Bigger display serif titles help, but it is a near-duplicate of head-1. The Ready line is squeezed into a cramped bar on Status and fails to match the sibling pages.
The page-coloured count beside every serif title (6, 5, 4, 9) and the legend caps show up on every page. It is a content-level change with companion colour (cyan Plans, lemon To do) and no new neon.
The tile tray makes counts visible and the Status gauge is good, but the tabs have bare arrows and the Matrix cursor is back. It is the same page as today under a new header.
The lamp line, tallies and selects are small edits on the parent, and most of the card is unchanged. It is close to a duplicate of mut-7.
The pencil lines and end blocks are tasteful but thin. It is a near-duplicate of head-2, and the Status and Chat sheets are unchanged.
The row bands and lamp legend visibly help the schedule and list pages, and the bone-on-slate text is warm. It is still the same blueprint, and the bands are a little greyish.

The lit gauge on the Status head, the NOW lamp with its time glass on a lit rail, and the pilot lamp bring the tube's light back where it belongs. The surrounding page stays calm and grounded, though the Status head is tall.
The one-line heads save height and the numerals are better set. It is the Grid Console with less change per page, and the Home panel cannot be judged from these cards.
The gauge and lamps by shape are good ideas, but the brown manila ground and brass plates make a bronze costume.
The titled rule is a good element, but the brown ground and brass labels remain, and the rails read like the old brass underline.

It is the most different of all: Swiss grotesque type, huge thin numerals, rules in each page's colour and a charcoal ground. It changes content on every page. But the phosphor effect is gone, contrast is the lowest at 4.77, and 41 targets are under 44px.

fixes.suggestion: Keep the serif titles, titled rails, hatched past days and amber today cell. Add the gauge and lamp from mut-9 and put a little more halo on the NOW marker.
Keep the lit gauge, the NOW lamp with its time glass, and the pilot lamp. Make the Status head shorter, and give the needle a reason to show when spend is $0 (the ghost average).
Keep the coloured count beside the serif title. Give the unit a true small cap and make the cooler ground an actual visible shift, not three levels.
Keep the dated spine on To do and the week dial on Plans. Fix the cut-off Status tube and tame the extra weight of the Fraunces titles.

Keep the huge thin numerals, the section-coloured top rules on Settings and the flush-left grid. Bring back the halo on the mark, the Send button, the key word and the monitors, and lift the contrast and the small targets.
Keep the faint row band and the lamp legend. Drop the heavy blueprint caps and grid; they are too dense for a family page.
Cut the brown ground and brass plates. The titled rule and burst traces could survive on a neutral charcoal case.

judges.notes: Most of the field is two parent families (Desk Terminal, Track Diagram and Long Persistence on a steel-black case, and Blueprint) with small edits, and several are near-duplicates (mut-3 and head-1, mut-7 and head-2, mut-6 and mut-7). The Signal Catalogue family (head-4, mut-11, mut-12) is the bronze wash. The owner's test favours designs whose structure shows on every page, such as the Grid Console rails, the Track Diagram serif titles and spine, and the coloured counts. The CRT light comes back best in mut-9, where it is confined to the gauge, NOW lamp and pilot rather than spread over the page. Wild-1 is the one real alternative and is worth developing, but it needs the phosphor back and the contrast and target size fixed.

parts.what: Serif title with a page-coloured typed count and unit beside it, standing on the masthead rule
To do as a dated spine with nodes and a lit NOW; faint alternate-row band as a runner
Moving-coil spend gauge on a tube, lit needle with a ghost average-day needle
Section head as a serif title and icon on a thin rail in the section's colour
NOW as a round lamp on a lit rail with the time on its own glass; lamps drawn by shape as the runner
Show filter as a row of lit-dot keys with a squared search field and Filter key
